intro: Two pieces of kuih kosui are about 140 kcal (estimate). Most of the calories come from the flour and gula melaka, while the grated coconut adds a little fat.
diet: Yes, and it's one of the lighter kuih compared to fried ones. It has almost no oil, just quite a bit of sugar. Two pieces with teh O for tea time fit nicely in your budget. Just be careful, they're small and easy to overeat.
tips: Take 2 pieces and put them on a plate, don't eat straight from the box.
Choose kosui over fried kuih like karipap or cucur when you can.
Pair with a boiled egg or a glass of milk for some protein.

swap.name: 1 medium banana
swap.why: Natural sweetness with fibre, and fewer calories.

faq.q: What is kuih kosui made of?
faq.a: Usually rice flour, tapioca flour or wheat flour, gula melaka, air kapur (lime water) and a little salt. It's steamed and then coated in grated coconut.

faq.q: Why does kosui need air kapur?
faq.a: Air kapur gives it that soft, chewy texture. Without it, kosui can turn too hard or too mushy.
Best finished the same day because of the grated coconut. Without coconut, you can keep it in the fridge for a day.
